content.title: About
content.content: Bagel with raisins is a traditional ring‑shaped bread product with a dense crust and a soft interior, featuring sweet raisins folded into the dough. It combines the subtle sweetness of raisins with the characteristic aroma of caraway seeds often used in bagel recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bagels originated in Eastern European Jewish cuisine and became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
The classic preparation method involves boiling short dough rings in water with baking soda before baking, giving the bagel its distinctive chewy crust.
Raisins are usually pre‑soaked in hot water to become plump and aromatic before being incorporated into the dough.
Bagels are commonly served with cream cheese, smoked salmon, or simply butter.
In Russia, bagels with raisins are often found in bakeries during the New Year holiday season.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Both the raisins and the whole‑grain flour used in the bagel provide dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Raisins are rich in polyphenols, which help combat oxidative stress in the body.

items.title: Enriched with B‑vitamins
items.content: Bagel dough typically contains thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the dough and natural sugars from raisins offers a fast source of energy, making it a good pre‑exercise snack.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides iron, potassium, and magnesium, essential for normal bodily functions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Raisins increase the overall sugar level of the product, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Bagel with raisins is relatively calorie‑dense; excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional bagels are made with wheat flour, making them unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sulfur dioxide
items.content: Some raisins are treated with sulfur dioxide, which can cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bagel with raisins can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, sliced and spread with cream cheese, hummus, or nut butter. It also works well in sandwiches, paired with ham, vegetables, or avocado.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bagel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, keep it in the refrigerator (up to 5 days) or freeze, wrapped in plastic, for up to 3 months. Warm in a toaster or oven before eating.
